# SQL statement built from HTTP request data (Java)

`qualor:java/sql-injection` · Issue · Severity: High · [CWE-89](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/89.html) · OWASP Top 10: [A05:2025 Injection](https://top10.owasp.org/2025/A05_2025-Injection/), [A03:2021 Injection](https://top10.owasp.org/2021/A03_2021-Injection/)

## What it finds

<!-- begin: what-it-finds -->
SQL text built from HTTP request data (Jakarta Servlet, Spring MVC, Jakarta REST) and run through:

- JDBC: `Statement.executeQuery`, `executeUpdate`, `execute`, `addBatch`, and
  `Connection.prepareStatement` / `prepareCall` with a built statement text;
- Spring JDBC: `JdbcTemplate`, `NamedParameterJdbcTemplate` and `JdbcClient` methods that take SQL;
- JPA and Hibernate: `createQuery`, `createNativeQuery` and similar methods that take query text.

Request data means servlet request getters and annotated handler parameters (`@RequestParam`,
`@PathVariable`, `@RequestHeader`, `@RequestBody` objects, `@QueryParam`, `@PathParam`, ...).
<!-- end: what-it-finds -->

## Why it matters

<!-- begin: why-it-matters -->
When a value is pasted into SQL text, the database cannot tell it from the statement. A value such
as `' OR '1'='1` changes what the query selects; others read other tables, change or delete data,
or on some databases run commands on the database server.
<!-- end: why-it-matters -->

## Example

<!-- begin: example -->
**Noncompliant:** the customer name is concatenated into the query.

```java
package com.example.shop;

import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import org.springframework.jdbc.core.JdbcTemplate;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.GetMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestParam;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RestController;

@RestController
public class OrderController {
    private final JdbcTemplate jdbc;

    public OrderController(JdbcTemplate jdbc) {
        this.jdbc = jdbc;
    }

    @GetMapping("/orders")
    public List<Map<String, Object>> orders(@RequestParam String customer) {
        return jdbc.queryForList("SELECT id, total FROM orders WHERE customer = '" + customer + "'");
    }
}
```

**Compliant:** the value is a bound parameter.

```java
package com.example.shop;

import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import org.springframework.jdbc.core.JdbcTemplate;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.GetMapping;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RequestParam;
import org.springframework.web.bind.annotation.RestController;

@RestController
public class OrderController {
    private final JdbcTemplate jdbc;

    public OrderController(JdbcTemplate jdbc) {
        this.jdbc = jdbc;
    }

    @GetMapping("/orders")
    public List<Map<String, Object>> orders(@RequestParam String customer) {
        return jdbc.queryForList("SELECT id, total FROM orders WHERE customer = ?", customer);
    }
}
```
<!-- end: example -->

## How to fix

<!-- begin: how-to-fix -->
- Keep the SQL text constant and bind values: a `PreparedStatement` with `?` placeholders and its
  setters, the argument list of `JdbcTemplate` methods, named parameters, or JPA `setParameter`.
- For identifiers (a column to sort by), choose from a fixed allow-list such as a `Map.of(...)` of
  constants or an enum.
- Converting the value to a number (`Integer.parseInt`) also makes it safe.
<!-- end: how-to-fix -->

## Frameworks and APIs covered

- Jakarta Servlet
- Spring MVC
- Jakarta REST (JAX-RS)
- JDBC
- Spring JDBC (JdbcTemplate)
- Jakarta Persistence (JPA)

## Known limits

<!-- begin: known-limits -->
- A handler parameter without an annotation is not a source. That misses a Spring MVC simple-type
  parameter (`String term`), which Spring binds from the request, and the Jakarta REST entity
  parameter (the request body).
- Only scalar types count as safe: an enum, a `List<Long>` or an `Optional<Long>` parameter is
  still reported, although it cannot carry SQL.
- A value added to a list (`List.add`) does not make the list request data.
- One method is analysed at a time: a helper of the same class that returns a constant still
  passes request data on, and a wrapper class in another file that reads the request is not a
  source. Conditions are not evaluated either.
- A `JdbcTemplate` whose type is not visible (a static field of another class) is checked only when
  its argument visibly starts as SQL; a query assembled otherwise (a `StringBuilder`) is missed
  there.
- Allow-list lookups are recognised only as `Map.of(...)` of constants read with `get` or
  `getOrDefault`, and as `valueOf` of an enum declared in the same file.
<!-- end: known-limits -->

## Tests

The test file [`rules/java/sql/sql-injection.java`](../../../rules/java/sql/sql-injection.java) holds every case the rule reports or accepts:
lines marked `ruleid:` must be reported and lines marked `ok:` must not. The known limits are
marked `todoruleid:` (missed) and `todook:` (wrongly reported). `npm test` runs them with OpenGrep,
and checks the example above as well.

The rule: [`rules/java/sql/sql-injection.yml`](../../../rules/java/sql/sql-injection.yml), added in version 2026.10.0.
